correctness.rationale: Proof in RESULT.md establishes the polar-vertex tight-incidence rank criterion, bipartite odd-parity saturation, the possible missing-edge gap 1 or 3, unique forced form for gap-three potentials, exact counting (with the two constant-overlap cases), and all-orbit classification by true graph automorphisms plus sign. Exhaustive standard-library code verifies 72 graph families by spanning-tree increments, independently tests full slack-permitting polar rank in the smallest cases, and checks all actual orbit-size multisets for 52 parameter triples. The mathematical proof is universal; finite tests are corroboration only. Domain p,q>=3, 0<=k<=min(p,q), real unit graph metrics.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general bipartite criterion implies every surviving edge must be tight, but does not enumerate homomorphisms for a rectangular biclique with a partial matching removed. The complete bipartite theorem handles k=0, not k>0. The crown record handles p=q=k only. This work supplies the nontrivial gap-three classification and orbit stabilizers in the uncovered regime.

originality.rationale: The proposed new statement is exact facet-additivity and the complete group-orbit classification for rectangular K_{p,q} with arbitrary partial matching deletions, not the established complete-bipartite count or the balanced full-matching crown case. The inspected original arXiv:1807.07678 Proposition 3.4 covers only k=0; the 2026 crown inradius record substantially covers p=q=k; the general bipartite tight-edge and facet-subgraph criteria need a separate gap-three uniqueness argument and group-action analysis before they give the proposed three-parameter classification. Braun–Bruegge small-graph tables are not general coverage. Semantic searches returned related but non-dominating statements. Residual risk: unindexed equivalent formulas and special isolated exact counts.
residual_risks: Full coverage cannot be excluded in unindexed, newly published, or inaccessible theses/datasets. Searches are evidence, not uniqueness proof.
The crown p=q=k balanced special case and k=0 baseline are not separate novel contributions; they are explicitly identified as prior-covered components.
Small isolated counts for at most seven vertices may appear in prior exhaustive graph tables; only the general full three-parameter classification and all orbit sizes are asserted as new.

value.rationale: For this canonical dense-to-near-dense metric perturbation, deleting k disjoint edges could in principle couple through all global polar constraints. The theorem proves a sharp unexpected noninteraction: exactly two exceptional facets per missing edge, classifies their forcing mechanism, and gives complete orbit representatives/sizes under the changed automorphism group for all rectangular dimensions and all intermediate deletions. This is a natural infinite-family structural and symmetry classification, neither an unmotivated numerical slice nor merely the known complete-bipartite/crown formula.
